cases.section: Primary remission with treatment alpha versus placebo at 8 weeks
cases.source: In a randomized trial, adults with condition delta received treatment alpha or placebo for 8 weeks. The primary outcome was remission at 8 weeks. Remission occurred in 40% with treatment alpha and 38% with placebo. The difference in the primary outcome was not statistically significant. The trial did not establish equivalence between treatment alpha and placebo. Follow-up was limited to 8 weeks, and longer-term remission was not assessed. The trial excluded children and adults receiving another investigational treatment. Remission was assessed using the same protocol in both treatment groups. Outcome assessors recorded remission at the planned follow-up visit. Missing observations were retained in the study records for review, and the report did not provide a separate estimate for participants with missing observations. Applicability outside the trial population remains uncertain.
cases.editorial: For adults with condition delta, the randomized trial compared treatment alpha with placebo over 8 weeks. The primary outcome, remission at 8 weeks, occurred in 40% with treatment alpha and 38% with placebo. The difference in the primary outcome was not statistically significant; equivalence between treatment alpha and placebo was not established. Follow-up was limited to 8 weeks, with longer-term remission unassessed. Children and adults receiving another investigational treatment were excluded. Both groups underwent remission assessment using the same protocol at the planned follow-up visit. Missing observations remained available in the study records, but no separate estimate was reported for participants with missing observations. Applicability beyond the trial population remains uncertain.

cases.section: Limitations of observational treatment alpha evidence
cases.source: A narrative review considered treatment alpha for adults with condition delta. The review described observational evidence and did not establish causation. The review noted selection bias and uncertainty about applicability. Differences between the included populations prevented a single comparative estimate. The review did not recommend treatment alpha as standard care. Treatment decisions were outside the scope of the review.
cases.editorial: For adults with condition delta, the narrative review describes observational evidence concerning treatment alpha. Causation was not established. Selection bias and uncertain applicability limit interpretation, while differences between included populations prevented a single comparative estimate. Treatment alpha was not recommended as standard care; treatment decisions remained outside the review's scope.

cases.source: For adults with condition delta, the panel suggests treatment alpha after shared discussion. The recommendation is conditional, with low certainty of evidence.
